## Q1
The incremental model of software development is\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

## Q1 - Options
(A) A reasonable approach when requirements are well defined.
(B) A good approach when a working core product is required quickly.
(C) The best approach to use for projects with large development teams.
(D) A revolutionary model that is not used for commercial products.

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q80

The incremental model delivers a working core product first and then adds features in successive increments, which is exactly why it fits situations where a client needs something usable quickly rather than waiting for the full system.

This approach does not require requirements to be fully defined upfront, since later increments can absorb evolving needs, it is not specifically tied to large teams, and it is a well-established, widely used commercial development model rather than a purely theoretical one, which rules out the other three options.

## Q2
The primary objectives of the SWE-IPT are to:

A. Solicit stakeholder needs and expectations.<br>
B. Specify the software requirements for the product and post-development processes.<br>
C. Generate the integrated technical plans for accomplishing the software development effort.<br>
D. Translate stakeholder requirements into a complete, specified architectural description.<br>
E. Ensure that the software technical data package is sufficiently detailed to facilitate an efficient and effective software implementation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q2 - Options
(A) All the statements are correct.
(B) Only B & C are correct.
(C) Only A & E are correct.
(D) Only C, D & E are correct.

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q87

A Software Engineering Integrated Product Team (SWE-IPT) is responsible for the full span of turning stakeholder needs into a deliverable, detailed software product.

- **A. Solicit stakeholder needs and expectations** — true, the starting point of the team's mandate.
- **B. Specify software requirements for the product and post-development processes** — true, translating needs into formal requirements.
- **C. Generate integrated technical plans for the development effort** — true, coordinating how the work gets done.
- **D. Translate stakeholder requirements into a complete architectural description** — true, turning requirements into design.
- **E. Ensure the technical data package supports efficient implementation** — true, the final handoff to implementation.

Each of these is a standard, complementary part of an integrated product team's mandate rather than a competing alternative, so the correct option is that all the statements are correct.

## Q3
Which of the following is not a Non functional requirement?

## Q3 - Options
(A) Portability
(B) Security
(C) Scalability
(D) User interaction

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q21

Non-functional requirements describe quality attributes of a system such as how portable, secure, or scalable it is, rather than what the system does.

Portability, security, and scalability are all quality attributes. User interaction describes what the system does for the user, a functional requirement, so it is the one that does not belong.

## Q4
How do you create agile processes to manage unpredictability?

A. Requirements gathering must be conducted very carefully.<br>
B. Risk analysis must be conducted before planning takes place.<br>
C. Software increments must be delivered in short time periods.<br>
D. Software processes must not adapt to changes incrementally.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q4 - Options
(A) A only
(B) B only
(C) C only
(D) D only

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q53

Agile methods are built specifically to manage unpredictable requirements, and their defining mechanism is short, frequent delivery rather than heavy upfront analysis.

Delivering software increments in short time periods lets the team get feedback and adjust direction quickly, which is exactly how agile processes cope with unpredictability.

Heavy upfront requirements gathering or pre-planning risk analysis are hallmarks of plan-driven approaches, not agile ones, and refusing to adapt incrementally is the direct opposite of what agile processes do.

## Q6
If every requirement can be checked by a cost – effective process, then SRS is called

## Q6 - Options
(A) Verifiable
(B) Tracable
(C) Modifiable
(D) Complete

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q26

An SRS is verifiable when every stated requirement can be checked by a finite, cost-effective process, such as a test, inspection, or demonstration, to confirm the software actually satisfies it. Traceability is about linking requirements to their origin and to downstream artifacts, and completeness is about covering all needed functions, neither of which is about checkability at reasonable cost.

## Q7
The process to gather the software requirements from client, analyze and document is known as:-

## Q7 - Options
(A) Software Engineering Process
(B) User Engineering Process
(C) Requirement Elicitation Process
(D) Requirement Engineering Process

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q29

Elicitation is only the gathering step, but this question describes three activities together, gathering, analyzing, and documenting, which together define the broader Requirement Engineering Process. Requirement Engineering encompasses elicitation, analysis, specification, and validation, so it is the correct name for the combined activity described here rather than elicitation alone.

## Q8
The model in which the requirements are implemented by its category is

## Q8 - Options
(A) Evolutionary Development Model
(B) Waterfall Model
(C) Prototyping Model
(D) Iterative Enhancement Model

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q32

The Iterative Enhancement Model groups requirements into categories and implements the software in successive increments, each iteration adding one category's worth of functionality on top of what was already built. Evolutionary development instead grows a working system through repeated prototypes shaped by user feedback rather than pre-grouped requirement categories, and the waterfall and prototyping models build the whole requirement set in one linear pass or one exploratory prototype respectively.

## Q9
Consider the following related to Fourth Generation Technique (4GT):<br>
A. It controls efforts.<br>
B. It controls resources.<br>
C. It controls cost of development.<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q9 - Options

(B) (B) and (C) only
(C) (C) and (A) only
(D) All (A), (B) and (C)

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q58

4GT tools dramatically shorten development time, but without discipline that speed can hide poor engineering practice. The standard caution about 4GT is that effort, resources, and cost of development must all still be actively controlled and measured, exactly as in any other process model, rather than left unmanaged just because the tools are fast. All three, effort, resources, and cost, are the things 4GT still needs to control.

## Q10
A good software requirement specification does NOT have the characteristic

## Q10 - Options
(A) Completeness
(B) Consistency
(C) Clarity
(D) Reliability

## Q10 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q84

The standard characteristics of a good SRS are correctness, completeness, consistency, clarity (unambiguity), verifiability, modifiability, and traceability. Reliability describes a quality of the running software system itself, not a property used to judge whether a requirements specification document is well written, so it is not one of the recognized SRS characteristics.

## Q11 - Options

(B) diagrammatic
(C) mathematical
(D) computer code

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** C

**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q13

## Q12
If every requirement stated in the Software Requirement Specification (SRS) has only one interpretation, then the SRS is said to be:

## Q12 - Options
(A) correct
(B) consistent
(C) unambiguous
(D) verifiable

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q14

An SRS is unambiguous when every requirement has exactly one interpretation. Consistency means requirements do not conflict; correctness means each requirement is one the system must meet; verifiability means each can be checked.

|---|---|
| A. Waterfall Model | I. Software can be developed incrementally |
| B. Evolutionary Model | II. Requirement compromises are inevitable |

**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q17

Waterfall rigidly partitions the project into sequential stages (IV). The Evolutionary model builds software incrementally through iterations (I). ## Q14
Statement I: The Cleanroom software process model incorporates the statistical quality certification of code increments as they accumulate into a system.<br>
Statement II: Cleanroom software engineering follows the classic analysis, design, code, test and debug cycle, focusing on defect removal rather than defect prevention.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q14 - Options
(A) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(B) Both Statement I and Statement II are false
(C) Statement I is true but Statement II is false

## Q14 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q19

Cleanroom does use statistical usage testing to certify each code increment (Statement I true). But its philosophy is defect prevention through formal specification and correctness verification, deliberately avoiding the traditional code-and-debug cycle, so Statement II is false.

## Q17
Which of the following is not one of the principles of agile software development method ?

## Q17 - Options
(A) Embrace change
(B) Customer involvement
(C) Following the plan
(D) Incremental delivery

## Q17 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q23

The Agile Manifesto explicitly values responding to change over following a plan.

- Agile methods emphasize flexibility, user collaboration, and continuous adaptation rather than rigid adherence to a predetermined project plan.
- Embracing change (Option A), customer involvement (Option B), and incremental delivery (Option D) are foundational agile principles.
- Following the plan (Option C) represents the traditional waterfall approach, making it the correct answer to the negative question.

## Q18
Which of the following statements is/are false ?

P : The clean-room strategy to software engineering is based on the incremental software process model.<br>
Q : The clean-room strategy to software engineering is one of the ways to overcome “unconscious” copying of copyrighted code.

Choose the correct answer from the code given below :<br>
Code :

## Q18 - Options
(A) Neither P nor Q
(B) Q only
(C) Both P and Q
(D) P only

## Q18 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q46

Both statements describe recognized definitions and applications of cleanroom software engineering.

- Statement P is true because Cleanroom software engineering structures development as a pipeline of increments, using formal specification, box structures, and statistical verification without unit testing.
- Statement Q is true because cleanroom design (Chinese wall technique) isolates developers from examining proprietary or copyrighted source code to prevent unconscious infringement during reverse engineering.
- Because both statements P and Q are true, neither statement is false (Option A).

## Q19
The Software Requirement Specification (SRS) is said to be \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ if and only if no subset of individual requirements described in it conflict with each other.

## Q19 - Options
(A) Consistent
(B) Unambiguous
(C) Correct
(D) Verifiable

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q53

By IEEE 830 standards, an SRS is defined as consistent if and only if no subset of individual requirements described within it conflict with one another.

- Consistency requires that no two statements define contradictory system states, terms, behaviors, or constraints.
- Unambiguous (Option B) means that every stated requirement possesses only a single unique interpretation.
- Correct (Option C) means every stated requirement represents an actual customer need.
- Verifiable (Option D) means there exists a cost-effective finite process to demonstrate that the software meets each requirement.
